transformation: double-buffer mvin/compute overlap
notes: DBUF kernel PASSES (oracle C_out_bf16 check). Split tiles_K=16 into 2 K-halves in disjoint spad banks (A:[0,1024)/[1024,2048), B-top:8192/7168), issued loop0(ex_accumulate=false)->half1 mvins(no fence)->loop1(ex_accumulate=true). Util: baseline 16384/36577=44.8% vs DBUF 16384/36730=44.6% (+153 cyc, 0.4% WORSE). DIAGNOSIS: no overlap win because the LEGAL baseline ALREADY overlaps loads w/ compute via Gemmini ROB. PROBE variant (fence after all-mvin) measured LOADCYCLES=20703, total-serial=43594 => pure compute~22891. Baseline 36577 < 43594 serial => baseline already recovers ~7k cyc of overlap. Since loop_ws_spad uses skip-loads(0x38)+spad_only(0x200), the loop ctrl's own ldA/ldB issue NOTHING; loads come from explicit host gemmini_extended_mvin, and ROB tracks spad-addr deps so K=0-tile compute starts as soon as its tiles land (does NOT wait for all mvins). Baseline 'issue ALL mvins then ONE loop' gives ROB MAXIMAL reorder freedom; DBUF's strict load0->compute0->load1->compute1 is MORE constrained program order, so it can't beat baseline (and is marginally worse). concurrent_loops=2 / a_spad_id/b_spad_id ping-pong is INERT here: spad_only(0x200) makes EX use literal a_addr_start/b_addr_end and ignore a_ex_spad_id (LoopMatmul.scala:1251-1254). True overlap ceiling ~max(20703,22891)~=23k; reaching it needs either DRAM-bandwidth reduction (loads are ~as costly as compute) or a schedule the ROB can't already extract -- not available via K-split double-buffering in spad_only mode.
